title: BA1/2686/2019 of RAJNI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
1ST Bail Application No. 2686 of 2019
Rajni ...Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent
Advocate: Mr. Abhishek Verma, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Deputy Advocate General along with Mrs.
Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
The present bail application has been preferred by the
applicant, who is shown to be an accused for commission of offence
under Sections 302, 34, 201 & 120-B of IPC, as registered against
her at P.S. Kunda, District Udham Singh Nagar; by way of an FIR
being FIR No. 04 of 2019. The complainant, who had registered the
application on 15.01.2019, is the brother of the deceased Vinod
Kumar. The deceased brother of the complainant had solemnized the
second marriage with the present applicant after the death of his first
wife.
2. The allegation levelled in the FIR against the applicant is that
the present applicant during the subsistence of her marriage with the
deceased Vinod Kumar had entered into an illicit relationship with
the neighbour named as Mohd. Nafis, and it is contended by the
prosecution that Mohd. Nafis, the present applicant and one Mr.
Sanjay had hatched the conspiracy, in plotting the murder of the
deceased Vinod Kumar. The complainant's case in the FIR; was that
the deceased brother was working as a Class IV employee and he
used to reside alongwith his wife and children at Serverkheda. It was
alleged by the complainant that his brother after the death of his first
wife, he entered into a second marriage with the present applicant. It
was contended that on 20.01.2019, the body of deceased Vinod
Kumar was found to be lying near Kunda Petrol Pump and it was
alleged that somebody has murdered him and later on had thrown his
body near the aforesaid place from where it was recovered.

2
3. After the registration of the FIR, the name of the present
applicant alongwith her paramour Mr. Mohd. Nafis, was disclosed to
have engaged in commission of the offence at their own residence,
and that the presence of both the persons, are shown in the residence
and it was after murdering the deceased Vinod Kumar; his body was
taken in a car and thrown on the road near the aforesaid petrol pump.
4. The investigation was carried by the Investigating Officer and
the involvement of the present applicant and Mohd. Nafis; alongwith
one Sanjay, is shown to have been established. Consequently, the
present applicant was arrested on 17.01.2019. Since then, she is
languishing in jail.
5. The applicant's case in the present bail application is that the
set of narration of the allegations in the FIR; do not make out a case
against her because she is not named therein the FIR, and even as per
the inquest report and after the post mortem which was conducted on
the deceased Vinod Kumar on 15.01.2019, the concerned doctor,
who conducted the post mortem, the cause of death, which is shown
to be is a haemorrhage, shock accompanied with asphyxia. The post
mortem report refers that there are about as many as 10 injuries,
which were suffered by the deceased on his body, including the
injuries caused by sharp weapon and abrasions. He submitted that
even on the perusal of the post mortem report, it cannot be inferred
that the wounds suffered by the deceased, which has resulted into his
death, was on account of an assault made upon him by the applicant
by the use of knife, which is complained of against her. He submits
that since there was no definite opinion expressed with regard to the
cause of death, she would be entitled to be granted bail, coupled with
the fact that there is no credible evidence available against her and
no motive has been attributed or established against her to commit
the offence under Section 302 IPC, and further that she would be
entitled for a parity because co-accused Mohd. Nafis @ Bablu, who
is alleged to be having an illicit relationship with her has been
granted bail by the order dated 08.11.2019.

3
6. He further submitted that the story of the prosecution of
recovery of knife on the pointing out of the applicant may itself not
lead to an inference that she was indulged in commission of the
offence, particularly, when according to the arguments of the counsel
for the applicant, Mr. Abhishek Verma, no stab injury is shown to
have been suffered by the deceased Vinod Kumar on person, and
hence the recovery of knife would be immaterial. He further submits
that since the applicant has got no previous criminal history and
there is no independent witness too, the applicant would be entitled
for bail.
7. Before venturing further, at this stage, this Court feels it to be
necessary to point out that the copy of the post mortem report, which
was filed by the applicant as Annexure no.2 to the bail application,
on its page 1 shows the details of the injury, including the two
injuries, which are shown and described to have been sharp
penetrating wound, which is reproduced hereunder:-
"Sharp superficial cut injury 4cm below Lt. ear,
horizontal external up of mouth 5 cm long.
Abrasion over lower lip Lt. side size 3 cm x 0.5cm.
Sharp penetrating wound size 1.5 cm x 0.3 cm at Lt.
side of neck 2 cm above Lt. clavicle. It extetnd
horizontal and penetrate fracture, length of penetrate in
7 cm. Lt. coastal artery and jugular vein cut,.....present
along whole length of injury"
8. For the reasons best known to the counsel for the
applicant, the typed version of the post mortem report, which has
been annexed with the present bail application does not show the
details of the injuries, which has been otherwise actually detailed in
the original post mortem report, which is quoted above. Hence, it
cannot be ruled out that the applicant has not come up with the clean
hands before this Court and had attempted to mislead the Court.
9. Even the parity, which has been claimed by the
applicant from the bail order dated 08.11.2019, as granted by the

4
coordinate Bench of this Court in Bail Application No.1426 of 2019
to paramour Mohd. Nafis, it was exclusively on the ground that no
one was named in the FIR and since it was the contention of the
applicant therein i.e. Mohd. Nafis that he has been falsely implicated
on the basis of the confessional statement of Rajni, the applicant
herein and further, since the Court was satisfied that the cause of
death was on account of a road accident, Mohd. Nafis was granted
bail. If the entire records, which have been placed before this Court
is taken into consideration, there would be no case of grant of parity
for grant of bail to the present applicant with Mohd. Nafis for the
reason being that his name itself was disclosed by the present
applicant to be indulged in commission of an offence and
furthermore, the Court was not made aware at that point of time
when the bail was being considered; and that it is no one's case that
the cause of death of deceased Vinod was on account of a road
accident. Hence, this Court declines to accept the arguments
pertaining to parity.
10. Coming to the order of rejection dated 18.11.2019, as passed
by the Court of I
st Additional District Judge/Additional Sessions
Judge, Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar. The reason for
rejection was that it was a conspiracy which was hatched by Mohd.
Nafis, his friend Sanjay and Rajni, i.e. applicant herein. The reason
assigned in the order further was that since it was on her pointing out
that the knife, which was used in commission of offence, committed
in the night of 14.01.2019, which was recovered on her pointing out,
the bail was rejected.
11. Another reason, which has been taken by the Sessions Court
for rejecting the bail was that Nafis and Sanjay took the body of the
deceased Vinod, in an Alto Car and thrown it on the road and there
was no one's case ever that there was a road accident, which was the
reason for the death of deceased Vinod Kumar due to the injuries
suffered by the road accident.

5
12. The bail application was preferred by the applicant on
15.12.2019 and the counter affidavit was directed to be filed by the
respondents/state. The Government Advocate has filed the counter
affidavit on 08.01.2020, and supplementary counter affidavit on
22.06.2020, annexing therewith the statement of the Doctor, which
was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.; as well as the recovery
memo of the articles, which had confirmed the view of the
prosecution that it was a deliberate and intentional murder caused by
the participation of the present applicant alongwith co-accused
persons.
13. The theory of the road accident and consumption of alcohol by
the deceased, it has been pleaded by the Government Advocate that
it is not made out, because the post mortem report does not show the
presence of alcohol, nor has the post mortem report, ever records that
the cause of death was on account of falling down. Learned
Government Advocate has taken a stand that since looking to the
nature of injuries, the deceased was strangulated after being stabbed
to death by a muffler, later on, the body of the deceased was
attempted to be disposed of. It would be necessary to consider the
recovery memo, which has been filed with the counter affidavit,
which shows that in the kitchen of the residence of the applicant
where the offence is alleged to have been committed, the blood
stains were found there and the FSL team had collected the samples
and had sent it for its scientific examination. Furthermore, it was
observed that blood stains were also found on the tiles of the kitchen,
which was broken and collected to be sent for FSL examination.
14. The recovery as shown on page 14 of the counter affidavit was
made on 17.01.2019 when the present applicant was taken by the
police team in the official car to the spot and after reaching at a
particular place she got the car stopped and in the presence of the
witnesses Rahat Ali and Mohd. Younus, she brought out the knife
where it was hidden which was used in the commission of offence to
have been buried in the ground in an adjoining vacant plot, which

6
she took it out herself after digging the mud by her hand. Hence, in
view of the evidence which has come on record by way of the
present counter affidavit, the presence of the applicant and her
paramour Mohd. Nafis, at the residence where offence was
committed is not ruled out and it further stand substantiated from the
call records, which had been placed in the supplementary counter
affidavit of the State which are the call details of the preceding date
of the incident and thereafter also, which shows that the paramour
Mohd. Nafis and the present applicant were in constant touch with
one another, which may lead to a logical inference that there was
some nexus between them in conspiring for commission of the
offence.
15. The learned Government Advocate has drawn the attention of
this Court to page 19 of the counter affidavit, which contains the
details of the call entries to establish that they were engaged in
consistent connection with one another at the time when the offence
was committed. As far as the aspect pertaining to the motive is
concerned, since the prosecution has specifically come up with the
case that the applicant was in an illicit relationship with Mohd. Nafis
and they both wanted to do away with deceased Vinod Kumar, it
cannot be ruled out their existing motive. Owing to the aforesaid and
after hearing the counsel at length, this Court is not inclined to grant
bail to the applicant. Hence, the bail application stands rejected.
16. Since these argument which had been dealt above pertains to
the documents placed on record in the bail application as well as in
the counter affidavit and supplementary counter affidavit and as they
were addressed in arguments by the counsel for the parties in order
to substantiate their respective cases, this Court didn't had any
option except to consider those arguments and recorded the
reasoning for not accepting the arguments; but, however the
consideration of the arguments made herein is expected not to
prejudice the minds of the trial, which is to be conducted
independently without considering or being influenced with the

7
findings recorded in today's order of rejection. The trial has to be
exclusively independent without being swayed with above reasoning,
which are exclusively for the purposes of bail only.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 10.07.2020
Mahinder/
